## 1. process.rs public surface + stop algorithm

Public functions in [viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/process.rs](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/process.rs):

- `pids_on_port(port: u16) -> Vec<Pid>` — [process.rs:23](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/process.rs) — finds PIDs listening on a TCP port via cascading tool fallback: PowerShell `Get-NetTCPConnection` on Windows ([process.rs:26-46](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/process.rs)), then `ss` ([process.rs:50-56](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/process.rs)), then `lsof` ([process.rs:58-66](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/process.rs)), then `netstat -ano` ([process.rs:68-75](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/process.rs)).
- `kill_process(pid: Pid, tag: &str) -> bool` — [process.rs:142](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/process.rs) — kills a PID, returns whether it's confirmed dead afterward.
- `process_exists(pid: Pid) -> bool` — [process.rs:167](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/process.rs) — checks liveness via `sysinfo::System`.
- `pids_by_image_name(package: &str) -> Vec<Pid>` — [process.rs:180](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/process.rs) — matches `sysinfo` process list by executable basename (`<package>` or `<package>.exe`, case-insensitive), independent of any port.
- `print_process_info(pid: Pid, tag: &str)` — [process.rs:199](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/process.rs) — prints `tasklist` (Windows) or `ps` (Unix) identifying info for a PID.

**Stop algorithm** ([process.rs:142-164](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/process.rs)): Windows path runs `taskkill /F /PID <pid>` once (already force-kill, no graceful step), sleeps 300ms, checks `process_exists`. Unix path first sends plain `kill <pid>` (graceful, SIGTERM), sleeps 500ms, checks liveness; only if still alive does it escalate to `kill -9 <pid>` (force), sleeps 500ms, and checks again. So there **is** a graceful→force escalation, but only on Unix — Windows always force-kills immediately. Every branch does verify termination via `process_exists` before returning.

## 2. Viewer-specific coupling

`pids_on_port` is entirely port-based; there is no name-only lookup inside `process.rs` itself, but `pids_by_image_name` ([process.rs:180-192](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/process.rs)) **is** a fully general by-executable-name path with zero port dependency — it's already usable for non-server binaries. The viewer-specific coupling lives in the **callers**, not in `process.rs`:

- [commands/server.rs:113-124](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/commands/server.rs) (`cmd_start`) frees the port via `pids_on_port(port)` before launch — assumes a `Server` config entry with a `.port`.
- [commands/server.rs:227-234](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/commands/server.rs) (`cmd_stop`, phase 1) kills by port, then [commands/server.rs:248-262](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/commands/server.rs) (phase 2) additionally calls `pids_by_image_name(&s.package)` to clean orphans not on the port — proving the name-based path is already exercised for server cleanup, just as a secondary phase.
- [commands/server.rs:212-224](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/commands/server.rs) `wait_for_port_ready` does an HTTP-adjacent TCP-connect health check — this is genuinely server/port-only and has no equivalent for a non-listening tool binary.
- [commands/mod.rs:200-217](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/commands/mod.rs) `cmd_prepare` stops by port then by image name.

**Verdict**: `process.rs` functions are already port-agnostic where it matters (`pids_by_image_name`, `kill_process`, `process_exists`, `print_process_info`); only `pids_on_port`/`wait_for_port_ready` are server-specific, and those simply wouldn't be called by an `install-ctl` that has no port to free.

## 3. Config model

[viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/config.rs:19-30](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/config.rs) — top-level `Config { defaults: Defaults, servers: Vec<Server>, frontends: Vec<Frontend>, extensions: Vec<Extension>, tasks: Vec<Task> }`, loaded from TOML file `<repo_root>/viewer-ctl.toml` ([config.rs:132-141](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/config.rs)) — **file-based, not hardcoded in Rust**. ```

Server { name: String, package: String, port: u16, source_dir: String, start_args: Vec<String>, env: BTreeMap<String, String> }

([config.rs:41-116](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/config.rs)). Repo root is resolved by walking ancestors of `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`/cwd for the `viewer-ctl.toml` marker file ([paths.rs:52-67](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/paths.rs)).

## 4. Build/Install logic

`build_server` ([commands/server.rs:37-49](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/commands/server.rs)) shells out to `cargo build --release --manifest-path <crate>/Cargo.toml`. `install_server` ([commands/server.rs:52-99](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/commands/server.rs)) prefers copying a pre-built `target/release/<package>[.exe]` binary to `$CARGO_HOME/bin` (or `~/.cargo/bin`), falling back to `cargo install --path . --force` run from the crate directory if no pre-built binary exists. Dispatch is per-component via `for_matching`/`cmd_build`/`cmd_install` in [commands/mod.rs:156-184](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/commands/mod.rs), which routes `Server`→`build_server`/`install_server`, `Frontend`→`build_frontend`/`install_frontend`, `Extension`→`build_extension`/`install_extension`.

## 5. Extension logic

Yes — `commands/extension.rs` already installs VS Code extensions ([commands/extension.rs:34-46](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/commands/extension.rs) `install_extension` dispatches on `e.kind == "vscode"`). `install_vscode_extension` ([commands/extension.rs:59-133](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/commands/extension.rs)) reads `package.json` for publisher/name/version to compute the `<publisher>.<name>-<version>` extensions-dir name, then: if the extension dir already exists under `~/.vscode/extensions`, syncs `out/`, `resources/`, `package.json`, `node_modules` in place ([commands/extension.rs:82-113](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/commands/extension.rs)); otherwise packages via `vsce package --no-dependencies --allow-missing-repository --skip-license` and installs via `code --install-extension <vsix> --force` ([commands/extension.rs:117-132](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/commands/extension.rs)). This is exactly the `vsce package` + `code --install-extension` pattern `install-extensions.sh` needs absorbed.

## 6. Reusability verdict + recommended organization

**Lift essentially unchanged**: `process.rs` in full (all five functions are already port- or name-based utilities with no viewer-registry dependency), `paths.rs` (`disp`, `copy_dir_contents`, `crate_manifest_path_str` are generic filesystem helpers), `shell.rs` (`run_cmd_args`/`which`, referenced from server.rs/extension.rs, not reviewed line-by-line here but used purely as generic subprocess wrappers), `commands/extension.rs`'s vscode installer logic (self-contained, no `Server`/port coupling beyond taking `&Extension`).

**Needs generalization**: `config.rs` — the `Component`/lookup model is sound but `Defaults.frontend_install_root` and the `Server.port`-centric shape are viewer-specific; an `install-ctl` config would need a parallel schema (e.g. a `[[binary]]` kind without a port) rather than reusing `Server` as-is. `commands/mod.rs`'s `for_matching`/`cmd_build`/`cmd_install` dispatch pattern generalizes well as a pattern but is typed against viewer's `Component` enum.

**Viewer-only, should stay**: `commands/server.rs`'s port-freeing (`pids_on_port`), `wait_for_port_ready` TCP health-check, and `STATIC_DIR`/frontend-linking logic — none of this applies to a bare installed binary like `mcp-toolmon`.

**Recommendation: option (a), a new shared crate** (e.g. `viewer-api/process-ctl` or a repo-root `tools/proc-ctl`) that both `viewer-ctl` and the new `install-ctl` depend on. Move `process.rs`, `paths.rs`, and `shell.rs` verbatim into it; keep `config.rs`'s `Config`/`Component`/`Extension`/`Task` shapes in the shared crate too since `install-ctl` will want the same TOML-driven extension/task model, but leave `Server`/`Frontend`/the STATIC_DIR/port-wait logic in `viewer-ctl` itself. Rationale: option (b) (copy) duplicates the Windows-handle-inheritance and PowerShell/ss/lsof/netstat fallback logic that took real effort to get right (see the Windows pipe-inheritance workaround at [commands/server.rs:389-409](viewer-api/viewer-ctl/src/commands/server.rs)), which will drift under maintenance; option (c) (generalize viewer-ctl, wrap it) forces `install-ctl` to carry the whole `Server`/port/STATIC_DIR concept it doesn't need. A shared crate keeps the port/health-check code exclusively where it's used (viewer-ctl) while giving install-ctl the process-kill, path, shell, and extension-install primitives without inheriting server-specific config fields.

## install-tools.sh
### CLI surface
- Positional tool names are accepted directly, and anything after `--` is also treated as a tool name; duplicates are deduped in memory ([install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L240-L301)).
- `--tool <name>` adds one tool, repeatable; `--tools <a,b,c>` adds a comma-separated list; whitespace inside the CSV is stripped ([install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L242-L257)).
- `--mcp` adds the MCP subset from `mcp_tool_names`; `--all` selects every supported tool in `tool_names`; `--list` prints the supported tool names and exits ([install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L258-L271)).
- `--dry-run` prints the cargo command without running it; `--no-force` removes the default `--force` passed to cargo install; `-h/--help` prints usage ([install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L273-L283), [install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L125-L165)).
- `INSTALL_TOOLS` is used only when no tools were selected on the CLI, and it is parsed as a comma-separated list ([install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L304-L310), [install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L155-L165)).

### Phases
1. Bootstrap and source shared shell helpers from `tools/install/common.sh` after locating the repo root with `BASH_SOURCE[0]` ([install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L1-L14)).
2. Declare the supported tool catalog plus the path/bin mapping functions that translate each tool name to a crate path and install binary name ([install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L16-L123)).
3. Parse CLI selection, apply `INSTALL_TOOLS` if needed, and fall back to installing everything when nothing was selected ([install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L240-L312)).
4. For each selected tool, build and run `cargo install --path <crate> --bin <bin>`, always with `--quiet` and normally with `--force`, under `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$repo_root/target/install-tools` ([install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L314-L355)).
5. Print the final summary via `installer_print_summary` and exit nonzero if any install failed ([install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L362-L369)).

- The catalog in [install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L16-L57) installs 24 artifacts. The mapping logic is in [install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L59-L123), and the actual cargo invocation is in [install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L314-L343).

### Process-stop handling today + exact failure point
- There is no process-stop or file-unlock logic today. The script only forces cargo to overwrite the install target by appending `--force` and then running the install command ([install-tools.sh](install-tools.sh#L324-L343)).
